newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina Senate bars back assessment of taxes.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina Senate bars back assessment of taxes.

text.p: The North Carolina Senate unanimously approved a proposal barring the state revenue department from trying to collect back payment for intangibles tax breaks that were retroactively ruled illegal.
The proposal, which passed the Senate on Thursday, still must be approved in the House and signed by the governor before it could take effect.

The U.S. Supreme Court ruled last year that North Carolina's intangibles tax on stocks and bonds was unconstitutional because it exempted the stock of in-state companies. The high court said that illegally interfered with interstate commerce.

The tax was eliminated by the General Assembly in 1995. The U.S. Supreme Court left it up to the North Carolina Supreme Court to determine whether refunds should be sent to everyone who paid the tax after the law was challenged in 1991, or if refunds should only go to those who paid under protest after 1991. The former would cost the state $400 million and the latter $155 million.

The state supreme court ruled that the state did not have to refund any of the money. It said the state could equalize the treatment of taxpayers by seeking back taxes from those who claimed exemptions for their in-state stock holdings.
Lawmakers said that would be political suicide because the exemptions were perfectly legal when they were claimed.
